How this book matches your board exam. Research check: this book follows NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 1 (Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants), for the CBSE 2026–27 session. The Biology theory paper is 70 marks in 3 hours, with 30 marks for practicals. Unit VI, Reproduction, carries 16 marks. It has three chapters: this one, Human Reproduction and Reproductive Health. Recent sample papers have 33 questions in five sections: A — 16 one-mark items (MCQs and assertion–reason); B — 5 two-mark; C — 7 three-mark; D — 2 four-mark case-based; E — 3 five-mark. Diagram questions are common in this chapter, especially the anther in transverse section, the anatropous ovule, the embryo sac and the stages of embryo development.

Each unit ends with a 10-mark practice set. The marking points are our own, not the official CBSE marking scheme. Chromosome-number answers were checked by computer.

Unit 1 of 10: The Flower and Pre-fertilisation Events

Key ideas

  • The flower is the site of sexual reproduction in angiosperms. Its reproductive whorls are the androecium (stamens, male) and the gynoecium (pistils or carpels, female).
  • Before a flower opens, a hormonal and structural sequence begins. Floral primordia form, and the inflorescence and flower buds develop.
  • Pre-fertilisation events are everything that happens before the gametes fuse:
  • development of the anther and pollen (microsporogenesis);
  • development of the ovule and embryo sac (megasporogenesis);
  • pollination;
  • pollen–pistil interaction.
  • In sexual reproduction, the gametes are haploid. Fertilisation restores the diploid number in the zygote, and seeds and fruits follow.
  • Flowers matter to people too: they are used as ornaments, in festivals, in worship, and to convey emotions such as love and grief.

Worked examples

Example 1: Name the two main pre-fertilisation structures in a flower. Answer: the stamen (produces pollen grains, the male gametophytes) and the pistil (contains ovules, which contain the female gametophyte).

Example 2: Put these in order: pollination, megasporogenesis, fertilisation, seed formation. Answer: megasporogenesis → pollination → fertilisation → seed formation.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) Which of these is the female reproductive part of a flower? (a) anther (b) filament (c) pistil (d) petal. Answer: (c).
  2. (1 mark) What is the collective term for all the stamens in a flower? Answer: the androecium.
  3. (2 marks) List any four events that happen before fertilisation in a flowering plant. Answer: any four, ½ each: anther and pollen development; ovule and embryo sac development; pollination; pollen landing and germinating on the stigma (pollen–pistil interaction); pollen tube growth.
  4. (3 marks) Distinguish between androecium and gynoecium on three points. Answer: male vs female whorl (1); made of stamens vs pistils or carpels (1); produce pollen grains vs contain ovules (1).
  5. (3 marks) Why are flowers called "the site of sexual reproduction" in angiosperms? Give three reasons. Answer: they carry the male and female reproductive organs (1); meiosis in anthers and ovules produces the haploid gametophytes (1); pollination, fertilisation and seed/fruit formation all happen in the flower (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Calling the pollen grain a gamete (it is the male gametophyte). 2. Mixing up "stamen" and "pistil". 3. Listing fertilisation as a pre-fertilisation event. 4. Forgetting that meiosis produces the spores, not the gametes directly. 5. Calling petals reproductive parts.

Quick recall

  1. Male whorl? 2. Female whorl? 3. Where does sexual reproduction occur in angiosperms? 4. Male gametophyte? 5. Ploidy of gametes?

Answers: 1) Androecium. 2) Gynoecium. 3) The flower. 4) Pollen grain. 5) Haploid (n).
